zh.q: 桌上这些器材各干什么？靠打点计时器那一端为什么要垫起来？
zh.concl: 本实验用槽码的重力当拉力（教材 p.88「小车所受的拉力可认为与槽码所受的重力相等」）、用纸带求加速度（p.89 方法 2）、用天平称质量（p.89）——装置就是图4.2-2 的参考案例 1。
points: 器材认得出：长木板一端垫高、滑轮在低的那一端、打点计时器在高的那一端、纸带从小车后端穿过限位孔。
三个量各有各的测法：质量用天平、拉力用槽码重力、加速度用纸带。
教材 p.89 旁注问「用测力计手拉行不行」——不行：手保证不了大小和方向恒定，也难与木板平行。

zh.q: 为什么要把木板一端垫高？垫到什么程度算「平衡好了」？垫过头会怎样？
zh.concl: 平衡阻力就是让重力沿木板的分量正好抵消摩擦（教材 p.90「使小车在不受牵引时能拖动纸带沿木板匀速运动」）；判据是纸带点距均匀，不是「垫一下就行」；垫过头会凭空多出 μ·g = 0.196 m/s²。
points: 平衡阻力要「不挂槽码 + 拖着纸带 + 能匀速」三个条件同时满足——只垫不挂纸带，纸带的摩擦没算进去，等于没平衡。
判据是纸带点距均匀（Δx = 0.00 mm），不是「垫了个东西」。
垫过头会凭空多出 μ·g = 0.196 m/s²，这一点第 7 步还要用。

zh.q: 先接电源还是先放小车？顺序错了，纸带上会少掉什么？
zh.concl: 教材 p.37「把小车停在靠近打点计时器的位置。启动计时器，然后放开小车……随后，立即关闭电源」；打点计时器用交流电源、50 Hz、每 0.02 s 一点，所以「每两个计数点间有四个点未画出」= 计数点间隔 0.1 s。
points: 顺序是「先接通电源、再放开小车」，最后「立即断电源」。
50 Hz → 0.02 s 一点；「每两个计数点间有四个点未画出」→ T = 0.1 s（不是 0.02 s）。
顺序错了的后果有数：开头空白 0.10 s ≈ 40 mm，可用间距 4 段 → 3 段、速度点 3 个 → 2 个。

zh.q: 一条纸带怎么变成一个 a？为什么不直接用 a = 2x/t²？
zh.concl: 相邻间距差恒定 ⟹ 匀加速；vₙ = (xₙ + xₙ₊₁)/(2T)（教材 p.23–24「用这一段的平均速度代表其中一点的瞬时速度」），三点连线的斜率就是 a（教材 p.37 的数据分析栏）。纸带已舍掉开头密集的点，起点速度 v₀ = 0.40 m/s ≠ 0，所以不能用 a = 2x/t²。
points: 相邻间距的「差」恒定才说明是匀加速；间距本身不恒定没有关系。
速度用前后两段的平均给中间那个点（教材 p.23–24「间隔越小越接近」）。
a 是 v–t 图的斜率，不是某个间距除以时间。

zh.q: 小车质量不变，多挂一个槽码，a 会变多少？五个点画出来是什么形状？
zh.concl: 控制变量：只改拉力时 a ∝ F；a–F 图线过原点（教材 p.91「如果这些点在一条过原点的直线附近，说明加速度 a 与拉力 F 成正比」），斜率就是 1/m。这五个数与教材表 4 逐位相同——其中 0.67 那一格教材是空的，是题目要你补的（按 a = F/m 算出来正好 0.67，这是答案，不是教材印的值）。
points: 控制变量：这一步只准动槽码个数，车上砝码块一块都不许动。
五个点要落在过原点的直线上，斜率就是 1/m（2.781 → 0.360 kg = 天平读数）。
点是「记录一组」存下来的，不是纸上自己画的——记 4–5 组就够。

zh.q: 固定拉力，把 a 对 m 画出来能看出什么？为什么教材要改画 a–1/m？
zh.concl: 双曲线不能直接判反比（教材 p.91「我们很难直观看出图线是否为双曲线」）；换成 a–1/m、若过原点即可判断 a ∝ 1/m（教材 p.92 原句）——这一步就是教材图4.2-4 → 图4.2-5 → 图4.2-7 的那次换轴。这五个数与教材表 5 逐位相同，其中 m = 0.31 kg 那一格是题目空格，补出来是 0.94（答案，不是教材印的值）。
points: a–m 图是双曲线，不能直接说「成反比」——必须换轴。
换轴以后要求「过原点」，不是「看着像直线」。
这一步只准动车上砝码块，槽码个数一个都不许动。
教材表 6 是同一个规律的 8 组数据：a·m ≈ 0.157 N，a–1/m 同样过原点（练习第 2 题）。

zh.q: 如果木板没垫好，或者槽码太重，a–F 图线会长成什么样？两种毛病在图上的样子一样吗？
zh.concl: 截距的符号就能判状态：与 F 轴交于正半轴 = 摩擦没抵消（没平衡好）；与 a 轴交于正半轴 = 垫过了头。槽码不满足「远小于小车」时，F = m_h·g 这条假设本身就不成立（教材 p.88 旁注「条件是槽码的质量要比小车的质量小很多」），表现为图线上端弯、由斜率求出的质量偏大。
points: 两种毛病在图上长得不一样：没平衡好 → 与 F 轴交于正半轴；垫过头 → 与 a 轴交于正半轴。
槽码太重 → 图线「弯曲」（不是平移），而且由斜率求出的质量偏大。
三种毛病都能用一个数说清：截距 ∓0.196 m/s²、偏差 −7.6 %，不是「误差大小看运气」。

zh.q: 只有槽码、纸带和一张坐标纸，能不能把小车质量测出来？
zh.concl: 没有新结论：把前七步连起来用一遍——控制变量（m 不变）+ 纸带测 a + 过原点直线斜率 = 1/m。这也正是教材 p.91「如果这些点在一条过原点的直线附近……」那句话的定量版。
points: 先按 k_F ≈ 1/m 估一下斜率，再看记的组数够不够。
要记就记同一个 m 的几组，换 m 会把斜率搞乱。
切到真实器材一定测不准——这不是你算错，是「槽码质量」这一项的系统误差。

en.q: What is each piece of equipment on the bench for? Why is the timer end of the board raised?
en.concl: This experiment uses the weight of the hanging masses as the pulling force (textbook p.88: "the pull on the cart can be taken as equal to the weight of the hanging masses"), the tape to find acceleration (p.89, method 2), and a balance to weigh the mass (p.89). The setup is reference case 1 in Fig. 4.2-2.
points: Recognize the equipment: one end of the board is raised, the pulley is at the low end, the timer is at the high end, and the tape passes through the guide hole from the back of the cart.
Each quantity has its own method: mass by balance, force by the hanging weight, acceleration by the tape.
A margin note on p.89 asks "could you pull with a spring scale by hand?" No: a hand can't keep the size and direction constant, nor keep it parallel to the board.

en.q: Why raise one end of the board? How high counts as "balanced"? What if it's raised too far?
en.concl: Balancing friction means the component of gravity along the board exactly cancels friction (textbook p.90: "so the cart, without being pulled, drags the tape down the board at constant speed"). The test is uniform dot spacing, not "just prop it up". Raising it too far adds a spurious μ·g = 0.196 m/s².
points: Balancing friction needs three conditions at once: no weights + dragging the tape + constant speed. Prop it up without the tape and the tape's friction isn't included, so it isn't balanced.
The test is uniform dot spacing (Δx = 0.00 mm), not "something is under it".
Raising too far adds a spurious μ·g = 0.196 m/s²; step 7 uses this again.

en.q: Power on first, or release the cart first? In the wrong order, what's missing from the tape?
en.concl: Textbook p.37: "Stop the cart near the timer. Start the timer, then release the cart… then switch off the power at once." The timer uses 50 Hz AC, one dot every 0.02 s, so "four dots not shown between counting points" means a counting interval of 0.1 s.
points: The order is "power on, then release the cart", and finally "switch off at once".
50 Hz → one dot per 0.02 s; "four dots not shown between counting points" → T = 0.1 s (not 0.02 s).
The wrong order has a measurable cost: 0.10 s ≈ 40 mm blank at the start; usable spacings 4 → 3, velocity points 3 → 2.

en.q: How does one tape become one value of a? Why not just use a = 2x/t²?
en.concl: A constant difference between successive spacings ⟹ uniform acceleration; vₙ = (xₙ + xₙ₊₁)/(2T) (textbook pp.23–24: "use the average velocity over this interval as the instantaneous velocity at a point within it"), and the slope through the three points is a (data analysis box, p.37). The dense dots at the start were discarded, so the starting speed v₀ = 0.40 m/s ≠ 0, which is why a = 2x/t² can't be used.
points: It's the constant *difference* between spacings that shows uniform acceleration; the spacings themselves needn't be constant.
Velocity at a point is the average over the segments on either side (textbook pp.23–24: "the shorter the interval, the closer").
a is the slope of the v–t graph, not one spacing divided by a time.
Work through the tape in Fig. 4.2-6 yourself: 6.19 / 6.70 / 7.21 / 7.72 cm, T = 0.1 s → Δx = 0.51 cm → a = 0.51 m/s².

en.q: With the cart's mass fixed, how much does a change when you add one weight? What shape do five points make?
en.concl: Controlled variables: changing only the force gives a ∝ F; the a–F line passes through the origin (textbook p.91: "if the points lie near a straight line through the origin, a is proportional to F"), and its slope is 1/m. These five values match textbook Table 4 digit for digit. The 0.67 cell is blank in the textbook as an exercise (a = F/m gives exactly 0.67; it's the answer, not a printed value).
points: Controlled variables: in this step change only the number of hanging weights; don't touch the blocks on the cart.
The five points should lie on a line through the origin whose slope is 1/m (2.781 → 0.360 kg = balance reading).
Points are stored with "Record", not drawn by hand; 4–5 sets are enough.

en.q: With the force fixed, what does a graph of a against m show? Why does the textbook switch to a–1/m?
en.concl: A hyperbola can't directly prove inverse proportion (textbook p.91: "it is hard to see by eye whether the graph is a hyperbola"); switch to a–1/m, and if it passes through the origin, a ∝ 1/m (textbook p.92). This step is the axis change from Fig. 4.2-4 → Fig. 4.2-5 → Fig. 4.2-7. These five values match textbook Table 5 digit for digit; the m = 0.31 kg cell is a blank exercise whose answer is 0.94 (not a printed value).
points: The a–m graph is a hyperbola; you can't say "inversely proportional" from it. You must change axes.
After changing axes, require "through the origin", not just "looks straight".
In this step change only the blocks on the cart; don't touch the number of hanging weights.
Textbook Table 6 gives 8 sets for the same law: a·m ≈ 0.157 N, and a–1/m also passes through the origin (exercise 2).

en.q: If the board isn't raised right, or the weights are too heavy, what does the a–F line look like? Do the two faults look the same?
en.concl: The sign of the intercept tells the state: crossing the positive F-axis = friction not cancelled (not balanced); crossing the positive a-axis = raised too far. When the weights are not much lighter than the cart, the assumption F = m_h·g itself fails (textbook p.88 note: "the condition is that the hanging mass is much smaller than the cart's mass"), so the line bends at the top and the mass from the slope comes out too large.
points: The two faults look different on the graph: not balanced → crosses the positive F-axis; raised too far → crosses the positive a-axis.
Weights too heavy → the line *bends* (not shifts), and the mass from the slope is too large.
Each fault can be stated as a number: intercept ∓0.196 m/s², deviation −7.6 %. Error is not "luck".

en.q: With only weights, a tape and graph paper, can you measure the cart's mass?
en.concl: No new conclusion: use the first seven steps together: controlled variables (m fixed) + tape for a + slope of the line through the origin = 1/m. This is the quantitative version of textbook p.91's "if the points lie near a straight line through the origin…".
points: Estimate the slope as k_F ≈ 1/m first, then check you have enough sets.
Record several sets with the same m; changing m will mess up the slope.
Real equipment will always miss: that isn't a calculation mistake, it's the systematic error from the hanging mass.
